summary: We developed a website which allows users to listen to unique audio experiences based on 2 examples of NASA Earth visualisations - one image was of aerosol mapping and the other was of global sea surface currents and temperature. Each colour translates to a different instrument and its shade determines the pitch. We tried our best to make the atmosphere of the music reflect our impression of the images. It addresses the challenge by making Earth science accessible to blind and visually impaired users through dynamic sonification. It is important because the beauty and wonder we get from new scientific discoveries and information about our world should be accessible to all.
details: Our project analyses the colours in 2 locally stored visualisations downloaded from the NASA resources tab. It assigns different instruments to different colours, and the hue of said colour determines the pitch of the sound; with lighter shades producing higher notes and darker shades producing lower notes. We sifted through a number of images before choosing 2 as we felt they represented the beauty of Earth science in separate ways while maintaining the same global map format. We wanted to maintain the same global format because for users with visual impairment, it offers a direct comparison about how viewing the image would have made them feel. The impact of the project is for users to feel wonder and emotional connection with the sound and be able to imagine the difference in state between the two chosen images i.e. the aerosol image felt more futuristic so we opted for a new age synth style audio with an atmospheric, electronic feel and the global sea surface currents image felt more fantasy-like, hence we opted for a more calming, flowing soundscape. We used Lovable AI and web-based technologies like Tone.js to produce our project. We considered accessibility features quite heavily e.g. font and colour options for colour-blind or dyslexic users, keyboard navigation throughout and labelled everything for text-to-speech screen reader compatibility, as well as emotional and artistic impact - we truly wanted to encapsulate how the visualisation made us feel and how this could translate to a similar experience for someone who is visually impaired. We also considered ease of use, clarity of the colour-to-sound mapping (ensuring there was no static) and the importance of creating distinct audio experiences.
